translations.Native Nextcloud-Administration erteilt: Native Nextcloud administration does not grant application-level access. An active app-local grant is required for protected calendar administration and domain demo data.

translations.Synchronisation is enabled by default. A: Synchronisation is enabled by default. As soon as shifts exist, AD Calendar creates the private calendar “%s” and transfers only your shifts; appointments and absences are not synchronised. You can disable synchronisation here. AD Calendar remains the source of truth: changes in the target calendar are overwritten and are not imported.
translations.Connect additional personal calendars. A: Connect additional personal calendars. AD Calendar creates the visible calendar “%s” with the provider and transfers only your shifts. Provider calendars are not displayed in AD Calendar; changes made by the provider are not imported.
translations.The Kopano provider must allow CalDAV ov: The Kopano provider must allow CalDAV over HTTPS. HTTP 405 means that the provider has not enabled CalDAV access at this address.
translations.These times appear as fixed shifts in th: These times appear as fixed shifts in the calendar and are suggested when creating an entry. Individually edited or deleted days remain single exceptions. If the end is before the start, the shift ends on the following day.
translations.Credentials are stored encrypted as a pe: Credentials are stored encrypted as a personal Nextcloud setting.
translations.The background job synchronises approved: The background job synchronises approved shift entries one-way from AD Calendar to personal DAV calendars. The technical structure remains open to a later bidirectional extension.
translations.No account or calendar identifiers are s: No account or calendar identifiers are stored or displayed in this status.
translations.The Kopano provider must provide CalDAV: The Kopano provider must provide CalDAV over HTTPS and forward methods such as PROPFIND to the Kopano CalDAV service. AD Calendar cannot enable this access on the external server.
translations.HTTP 405 means that the provider does no: HTTP 405 means that the provider does not allow a CalDAV connection at this address. Without credentials, HTTP 401 is an expected login request; a successful authenticated PROPFIND usually responds with HTTP 207.
translations.Personally saved server addresses remain: Personally saved server addresses remain unchanged. Existing app-owned calendars are renamed during the next successful synchronisation; technical calendar and object identifiers remain stable.
translations.The default %s remains editable in the p: The default %s remains editable in the personal connection dialog. If the published CalDAV address differs, enter the full HTTPS address there.
translations.The test performs only a read-only CalDA: The test performs only a read-only CalDAV request. Credentials are not stored and no calendar is created.
translations.This system-wide web client configuratio: This system-wide web client configuration allows all users to connect their own Google account in the personal settings tab.
translations.Register a Google app – step by step: Register a Google app – step by step
translations.A Google Cloud project is required for r: A Google Cloud project is required for registration. The following steps are performed once by an administrator:
translations.Select or create a project in the: Select or create a project in the
translations.Under APIs and services → Library, searc: Under APIs and services → Library, search for and enable the Google Calendar API.
translations.Under Google Auth Platform → Branding, e: Under Google Auth Platform → Branding, enter the app name, support email and contact address.
translations.Under Google Auth Platform → Audience, s: Under Google Auth Platform → Audience, select Internal if only accounts from the same Google Workspace organisation may access it. Otherwise select External. In test mode, add the intended accounts as test users; refresh tokens may then expire after only seven days.
translations.Under Google Auth Platform → Data access: Under Google Auth Platform → Data access, add exactly the scope
translations.It allows AD Calendar to access only sec: It allows AD Calendar to access only secondary calendars created by the app and their appointments.
translations.Copy the authorised redirect URI shown b: Copy the authorised redirect URI shown below using “Copy URI”.
translations.Under Google Auth Platform → Clients, cr: Under Google Auth Platform → Clients, create an OAuth client of type Web application and enter the copied URI exactly under Authorised redirect URIs. Do not add authorised JavaScript origins.
translations.Enter and save the Google client ID and: Enter and save the Google client ID and Google client secret here. The secret is not displayed afterwards.
translations.Users can then select Connect for Google: Users can then select Connect for Google under AD Calendar → Settings → External calendars.
translations.The protocol, domain, path and any trail: The protocol, domain, path and any trailing slash of the redirect URI must match exactly. Google may additionally require verification for an external production app.

translations.This URI must be entered exactly as an a: This URI must be entered exactly as an authorised redirect URI in the Google Cloud OAuth client.

translations.The secret is stored as sensitive and la: The secret is stored as sensitive and lazy Nextcloud AppConfig and is never displayed again.
translations.Removing the configuration deletes the c: Removing the configuration deletes the client ID and client secret from Nextcloud. User grants already issued by Google are not automatically revoked.
translations.The demo pack creates only synthetic loc: The demo pack creates only synthetic local accounts, local groups where required, and neutral shifts and appointments. It is not installed automatically and does not import existing WordPress data.
translations.Existing foreign accounts and read-only: Existing foreign accounts and read-only LDAP groups cause the operation to stop before the first change.
